t: Five dynasties of Turkic and Afghan origin ruled northern India from Delhi for 320 years, from 1206 to 1526.
It repelled repeated Mongol invasions and fostered the Indo-Islamic culture of the Qutb Minar and Amir Khusrau.
Overreach, provincial breakaways and Timur's sack of Delhi weakened it before Babur won at Panipat in 1526.
dyk: The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta served as a qazi, or judge, at the court of Muhammad bin Tughlaq in Delhi from 1334.
ev: Qutb ud-Din Aibak founds the Mamluk or Slave Dynasty after Muhammad of Ghor's murder
Abbasid caliph sends Iltutmish a diploma recognising him as sultan

Malik Kafur plunders the Pandya lands around Madurai
